ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT provisions are in Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and related regulatory provisions of the French Code monétaire et financier. Customer identification and beneficial-owner identification are principally governed by Articles L.561-5, L.561-5-1, L.561-6 and L.561-10. Beneficial-owner information and filing obligations are governed principally by Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and Articles R.561-1 to R.561-3 of the Code monétaire et financier, together with the French Commercial Code provisions governing the Registre national des entreprises. The register is maintained through the Institut national de la propriété industrielle under the legal framework introduced by the PACTE Law and subsequent implementing regulations. The beneficial owner is generally the natural person who directly or indirectly holds more than 25% of capital or voting rights, or otherwise exercises control under Article R.561-1. If no such person can be identified, the senior managing official is reported in accordance with Article R.561-1.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and onboarding, screen all founders, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, intermediaries, principal contractors and relevant counterparties against United Nations sanctions, directly applicable European Union sanctions, French asset-freezing measures under Articles L.562-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier, and applicable domestic restriction lists. Screen against OFAC lists as a contractual and correspondent-banking control where there is a United States nexus, dollar clearing, US person involvement or customer requirement; OFAC screening is not independently mandatory for every France-only transaction. Apply enhanced due diligence to politically exposed persons, family members and known close associates under Articles L.561-10 and related provisions. Verify source of wealth, source of funds, ownership/control, adverse media, corruption exposure, export-control exposure and beneficial ownership. Preserve screening evidence, risk ratings, approvals and transaction-monitoring records for the statutory retention period, generally five years after the end of the business relationship or transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name and entity data can also be checked through the Registre national des entreprises and Data INPI services
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be entered in the Latin alphabet for registry processing and must include or clearly identify the corporate form, such as Société par Actions Simplifiée or SAS. French diacritics may be used. A translated or transliterated commercial name does not create priority over an earlier French or European trademark, company name, trade name or domain name. Pre-clearance must cover the RNE, INPI trademark databases, EUIPO, domain names, trade names and relevant foreign registries. A name must not mislead the public as to governmental status, regulated activity, ownership, purpose or geographic origin.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: French governmental and public-authority designations, including République, France, Ministère, État and official institutional names, unless specifically authorized
Banking, credit, insurance, investment-services, payment, financial-market and other regulated-sector terms where use could imply an unauthorized regulated activity
Terms implying a public-service concession, official certification, sovereign authority, diplomatic status or statutory monopoly
Protected professional or regulated-activity designations, including avocat, notaire, expert-comptable, architecte and equivalent terms, unless legally entitled to use them
Geographic, national and international organization names where their use is misleading or requires authorization
Offensive, discriminatory, deceptive or public-order-incompatible expressions
Names identical or confusingly similar to existing registered companies, trademarks, trade names or domain names
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a universal statutory 30-day company-name reservation mechanism equivalent to some foreign jurisdictions; the 30-day period is a conservative project-management window for completing the filing after a name check. Submit the incorporation formalities through the Guichet unique with the proposed name, corporate-form designation, business purpose and supporting documents. If the filing is rejected, obtain the electronic rejection notice and reasons, correct the name or provide evidence of authorization and non-confusion, and resubmit through the portal. Where the decision is an appealable administrative decision, file a reasoned administrative recourse with the issuing authority within the applicable deadline, generally two months from notification, while preserving proof of filing. A judicial challenge before the competent administrative or commercial court may be considered depending on the legal nature of the decision. A rejected name does not protect the name against third-party use; obtain separate trademark and domain-name protection where commercially material.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a registered office in France under Articles L.123-11 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. A domiciliation company or virtual-office provider may be used if it is legally authorized, has a written domiciliation agreement, verifies the identity and authority of the client, and maintains the required records. A director's home may be used subject to statutory limitations and landlord, lease, condominium and local restrictions. A virtual office is generally unsuitable as the sole operational arrangement for offshore wind foundation installation because the activity requires project management, engineering, procurement, safety, maritime, environmental and contractor substance. Maintain accessible corporate records, a functioning French management interface, appropriate personnel or subcontracting arrangements, project documentation, insurance and operational evidence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official national probability is published. For a newly formed SAS in offshore marine construction, an internal risk estimate is approximately 5% to 15% for an unannounced physical inspection in the first three years, increasing materially if the company seeks public procurement, maritime authorizations, environmental approvals, tax refunds, employment registrations, customs activity or is subject to a complaint, AML alert or workplace-safety concern. This is an operational estimate, not a statutory probability or prediction.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), including Articles L. 210-1 et seq. (commercial companies), L. 227-1 et seq. (SAS), R. 123-1 et seq. (Trade and Companies Register), and Articles L. 561-46 et seq. (beneficial ownership information). The Civil Code applies to general contract and contribution matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Trade and Companies Register (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS), maintained by the clerk of the relevant commercial court; creation filings are submitted through the INPI Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company creation filed through the INPI Guichet unique, supported by the SAS articles of association (statuts); the filing results in RCS registration and issuance of a SIREN number and Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS; capital may be set in the articles, including at EUR 1. For cash contributions, at least 50% of each subscribed amount must be paid at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. Cash is deposited with a bank, notary, or other legally authorized depositary pending registration; the deposit is released after registration. Contributions in kind generally require a contribution auditor unless a statutory exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions for the shares set out in the executed articles of association and confirms that the required portion of each cash contribution has been deposited with the designated depositary. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full French address], as stated in the articles. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed President (Président) of the Company for the term and on the terms provided in the articles, and that [name] is appointed [officer title, if applicable]. The President is authorized to complete registration formalities, obtain the Company’s tax and social registrations, and execute documents necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises (formalities.inpi.fr); French notary where a notarial instrument is legally required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language articles specifying the corporate name, purpose, registered office, term, share capital, contributions, share rights, governance, and appointment method for the President. Obtain signatures from all founders. Use qualified electronic signatures or wet signatures; notarization is not generally required for ordinary SAS articles. Notarial formalities may apply to particular asset contributions or transactions.
required_dossiers: President's identity, acceptance of appointment, and non-conviction declaration
Contribution auditor report or exemption documentation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies in names, capital, purpose, or governance provisions; obtain missing signatures or reports; resubmit the amended instrument through the Guichet unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, notary, or other legally authorized capital depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a formation account and transfer at least 50% of subscribed cash contributions. Obtain the certificate of deposit (certificat du dépositaire des fonds) for the registration filing. Identify each subscriber and contribution consistently with the articles. Arrange release of funds after RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or draft articles accepted by the depositary
Proof of source of funds, if requested under AML requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve KYC or source-of-funds queries with certified identity and ownership records; correct the subscription schedule or transfer amount and obtain a replacement deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal announcements journal (journal d’annonces légales) for the registered-office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the prescribed incorporation notice after signing the articles and before submitting the registration application. Ensure the notice reflects the exact corporate name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, and President details. Obtain the publication certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected or supplementary notice and updated publication certificate if any statutory particulars are omitted or inaccurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises; competent local RCS clerk for examination and registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic company-creation filing with supporting documents and beneficial-owner information. Pay applicable registry and beneficial-owner filing charges shown by the portal. Respond to requests through the portal. Upon approval, verify the Kbis extract, SIREN/SIRET, and APE code; arrange release of deposited capital.
required_dossiers: Required authorization or professional qualification evidence, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address the clerk’s deficiency notice within the stated deadline by uploading corrected or additional evidence. If rejected, correct the identified formal defect and refile; use available registry review or appeal procedures where the refusal is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration tax and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), URSSAF, and relevant social-security bodies through their applicable online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm corporate tax and VAT treatment, establish accounting and invoicing systems, and complete employer and social registrations before hiring. Register for VAT and obtain any required intra-EU VAT number through the competent tax office. Maintain the RCS extract, beneficial-owner record, and statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Business activity and anticipated turnover information
Employee and payroll information, if hiring
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registration data with the relevant authority and provide supporting corporate or activity evidence; do not commence regulated operations or employ staff before applicable prerequisites are met.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No single national industrial licensing board grants a general offshore-piling contractor licence. Project and site authorizations are handled by the competent prefect (including the maritime prefect where relevant), with technical review by the relevant DREAL and other competent maritime, environmental, and construction authorities. The Ministry for Ecological Transition is the national policy authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general company-level operating licence applies solely because the SAS performs offshore wind-turbine piling. The specific offshore wind project requires applicable project authorizations, which may include an environmental authorization under the Environmental Code, authorization to occupy the public maritime domain, and other energy, maritime, or construction approvals. The contractor must also satisfy applicable construction, insurance, and site-safety requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition écologique), with examination by the competent environmental authority and relevant DREAL services; project decisions are made by the competent permitting authority, commonly the prefect.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening under Environmental Code Articles L. 122-1 et seq. and R. 122-2. Offshore wind farms and associated works generally require a project-level environmental impact assessment and public-participation procedures; a standalone contractor is not automatically subject to a separate company-level EIA. Confirm scope and screening with the competent authority before works.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single sector-wide numeric threshold applies to all piling works. Comply with the project environmental authorization, water and marine-environment requirements, applicable ICPE rules where a classified facility is operated, and permit-specific limits for discharges, noise, turbidity, emissions, and waste. Prohibit unauthorized discharges; segregate, characterize, and transfer waste to authorized operators; document monitoring and incident reporting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before mobilization, obtain required site-owner and project safety approvals, prepare the applicable prevention plan or coordination documentation, and comply with the Labour Code, maritime safety rules, and occupational risk-assessment duties. Fire-safety and structural approvals apply to relevant buildings, installations, and works under their specific regimes; there is no universal offshore-piling-company clearance. Verify vessel, lifting-equipment, occupational health, emergency-response, and site-specific inspections before work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the Ministry of Economy and Finance; official portal: impots.gouv.fr; business incorporation and tax ID registration performed via the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The French SAS is incorporated via the Guichet Unique, which triggers automatic RCS registration and sequential issuance of (a) a 9-digit SIREN as the French tax identification number, (b) a 14-digit SIRET establishment identifier, and (c) a French intra-Community VAT number (n° TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + 2-digit key + SIREN), all delivered electronically by the DGFiP through the INFOGREFFE / INSEE chain. A non-resident foreign entity with no permanent establishment in France must apply directly to the DGFiP for a non-established taxable person VAT number (assujetti non établi) by completing the DGFiP's specific registration procedure on impots.gouv.fr, providing certified identity documents, proof of the foreign tax registration, and appointing an accredited tax representative (représentant fiscal) if it seeks a VAT refund under the 13th Directive or performs taxable transactions subject to French collection duty. The SIREN is mandatory before issuing any domestic B2B invoice; alternatively, for imports/works received by a French VAT-registered customer, the parties may apply the reverse charge and the foreign entity need not register unless it undertakes local supply chains or owns a fixed establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' regime. An SAS is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level under CGI Art. 206. The principal statutory election mechanisms are: (a) option under CGI Art. 239 bis AA allowing a small-qualifying SAS to elect quasi-transparent taxation in the hands of shareholders for a non-renewable period of five fiscal years; (b) election for fiscal integration (régime d'intégration fiscale) under CGI Art. 223 A whereby a parent company owning directly or indirectly at least 95% of the SAS may form a consolidated French tax group; (c) notification/designation mechanics for hybrid mismatch arrangements under the ATAD, requiring filing of Form 2257-SD with DGFiP where the French entity participates in a structured cross-border arrangement involving hybrid entities or financial instruments; and (d) the VAT classification election for mixed supplies — the SAS must apply the predominant-purpose test under CGI Art. 258 to 259-D, with no independent ECI election, and may opt for the OSS regime only for intra-EU B2C digital and distance-sale transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No quantitative turnover threshold triggers registration for an SAS established in France: VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction. The only relevant ceilings are the optional VAT exemption thresholds (franchise en base de TVA): €85,800 per annum for predominant goods activities and €34,400 per annum for predominant services activities (thresholds revalorised every three years by decree), but these exemptions are unavailable in practice where the SAS supplies construction/installation services to VAT-liable customers subject to reverse charge. For a non-established foreign supplier of offshore installation services, registration is not required when the French customer self-accounting for reverse charge applies; for EU distance sales of goods to French consumers, the EU-wide €10,000 threshold for the One-Stop-Shop applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing structured e-invoicing and e-reporting reform. From 1 September 2026, large enterprises must transmit domestic B2B invoices through a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public portal (Portail Public de Facturation); SMEs must comply from 1 September 2027. Invoices must respect the EN 16931 semantic standard (Factur-X format minority). Transactions with foreign counterparties, including exports, require e-reporting of transaction and entity data rather than full e-invoicing. Customs exports are declared electronically in the DELTA-G system; France does not apply real-time fiscal stamping or continuous controls to VAT invoices, but DGFiP cross-references e-invoice data, customs declarations, and bank settlement records for audit matching.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.export_zero_rating_eligibility: Under CGI Art. 262-I-1°, a definitive exemption from VAT (zero-rating) with full input VAT recovery applies to goods physically dispatched or transported out of the European Union by the supplier or for the supplier's account. The supplier must hold objective evidence of export within 90 days from the time of supply (extendable by supporting justification). Offshore wind monopile and transition-piece installation contracts are composite supplies: the installation services are governed by the place-of-supply rules (CGI Art. 259 to 259-D) — where the wind farm is located inside French territorial waters or the exclusive economic zone, VAT is chargeable in France at the destination-country rule for immovable-property work; for B2B customers outside France, reverse charge is required; the zero-rating applies exclusively to the separable goods element that crosses the EU customs border under an export declaration. The zero-rate cannot be claimed merely on the basis of an international transport contract or incoterm; physical proof of arrival outside the EU must be shown.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DAU (Document Administratif Unique) lodged electronically in the DELTA-G customs system with a valid EORI number
Bill of Lading, seaway bill, CMR consignment note, or Air Waybill proving physical departure of the goods from EU territory

Commercial invoice issued by the SAS (or its sub-contractor) detailing the pilings/monopiles, quantities, unit prices, incoterms, and explicit mention of the 0% export exemption in accordance with French invoicing rules
Forwarding contract or shipping instructions evidencing that export transport was arranged by the supplier or on its behalf
Proof of payment, project financing wire advice, or Letter of Credit negotiation document linking the foreign counterparty and the export transaction (inward remittance certificate)
Where installation labour is bundled, a signed works completion certificate and a materials-value breakdown segregating goods from services for correct VAT treatment
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: In the event of audit, an unjustified zero-rating is reassessed at 20% VAT plus late-payment interest (intérêt de retard: 0.10% per month). A deliberate misstatement raises the civil penalty to 40% of the tax underpaid (manquement délibéré); bad-faith or fraudulent behaviour triggers an 80% penalty plus, in serious cases, the application of l'abus de droit under CGI Art. L64 LPF. If the exporter cannot produce the required export evidence within the 90-day period, the VAT becomes immediately payable and is revoked retrospectively. The DGFiP's audit statute of limitations is six years, extended to ten for cross-border fraud schemes, and criminal tax fraud under CGI Art. 1741 — knowingly issuing or using false export documents — is punishable by imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to €500,000, with ancillary bans on public procurement and corporate punishment under the French Criminal Code (Art. 131-39).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France’s central bank and participates in the Eurosystem. The Direction générale du Trésor (French Treasury) administers applicable foreign-exchange and financial-relations rules under the Monetary and Financial Code. The European Central Bank and applicable EU law govern relevant monetary and payment-system matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies the euro and, as an EU Member State, generally permits free movement of capital and payments under Article 63 TFEU, subject to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering rules, prudential requirements, tax rules, and specified security-related controls. There is no general requirement for prior approval to convert euros or remit dividends, interest, royalties, or sale proceeds abroad. Distributions remain subject to corporate-law requirements, available distributable profits, withholding-tax rules, treaty or EU relief procedures, beneficial-owner documentation, and bank checks. Cross-border payments may be reportable for balance-of-payments or statistical purposes; reporting is not ordinarily an exchange-control approval. The company should confirm transaction-specific reporting and documentation requirements with its bank and French advisers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio for ordinary commercial export receipts. Export proceeds may generally be retained in euros or foreign-currency accounts, subject to bank account terms, sanctions screening, tax and accounting obligations, and any applicable statistical reporting. Invoices, customs evidence, contracts, and payment-purpose information should be retained to substantiate receipts and payments.

Operational Account; Capital Deposit Account for SAS formation where accepted

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank

Operational Account; Capital Deposit Account for SAS formation where accepted

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. An EU-authorised electronic money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts and cross-border transfers under its passporting rights, subject to its permitted services, safeguarding arrangements, onboarding policy, and sanctions and AML controls. An EMI account is not necessarily a bank deposit and may not provide a French SAS formation capital-deposit certificate or the full credit, trade-finance, escrow, and letter-of-credit capabilities required for offshore-wind projects. Verify the provider’s authorisation in the relevant official register, account-holder and safeguarding terms, currency coverage, transfer limits, and SWIFT access. Non-EU providers must establish an applicable lawful basis to serve the French company; their services do not displace French and EU compliance obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal in-person director interview or physical-presence requirement for opening a corporate account. Banks set their own risk-based onboarding procedures and may require an in-person appointment, live video verification, certified documents, or a French-resident representative. Remote onboarding is possible at some institutions but is not assured, particularly for non-resident shareholders, complex ownership chains, high-value project flows, or trade-finance requests. For SAS formation, the capital deposit and receipt of the deposit certificate must follow the selected bank’s procedures before registration; the certificate is ordinarily used in the registration process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, trusts, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registers and constitutional documents for each ownership layer; certified or appropriately authenticated extracts; ownership chart through to natural-person beneficial owners; identity and address evidence; French beneficial-owner filing evidence where applicable; explanations and supporting documents for control rights and any nominee or trust arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, unusually large shareholder funding, or funds received from an unrelated or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription and shareholder-loan agreements; board or shareholder approvals; bank statements showing the funding trail; audited accounts, tax returns, sale agreements, or other source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; remitter identity and relationship evidence; payment purpose and bank transfer references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Project activity, counterparties, vessels, equipment, or payment routes implicating sanctions, export controls, or restricted end users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty and beneficial-owner screening records; vessel, port, and country details; sanctions and export-control classification; end-use and end-user statements; supplier and customer contracts; shipping and customs documents; documented escalation and approval records for any potential match.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, irregular, third-party, circular, or poorly described payments inconsistent with offshore-wind installation activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed project, supply, and subcontracting contracts; invoices and purchase orders; project budget and payment schedule; engineering or delivery milestones; proof of delivery or acceptance; reconciliation of payer and payee to contractual parties; written explanation of any agency, consortium, joint-venture, or third-party payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for project finance, escrow, capital-account treatment, or trade finance without a clear transaction structure or repayment source.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Project-company and group structure; concession, tender, or project-award documents; financing and security documents; construction and supply contracts; cash-flow forecast and sources-and-uses statement; insurance and permits; board approvals; lender and guarantor information; proposed account-control and disbursement arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the declared business, French company records, tax/VAT profile, and expected transaction volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract, articles of association, registered-office evidence, management and signatory mandates, tax and VAT registrations as applicable, business plan, staffing and operating-location information, expected annual turnover and transaction profile, and explanation of group or cross-border cash flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route share capital and shareholder funding from an account in the documented investor’s name to the designated French bank capital-deposit or corporate account, as applicable. Use a bank-to-bank SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within SEPA or a SWIFT transfer for other currencies or routes. State the accurate purpose as share subscription, paid-in capital, or shareholder loan; do not characterize debt as equity or vice versa. Provide the subscription or loan agreement, corporate approvals, investor identity and beneficial-ownership evidence, source-of-funds documents, and remitting-bank details. Reconcile receipt to the company’s ledger and obtain the capital-deposit certificate required for SAS registration when relevant. French banks may request payment-purpose and counterparty information and may report transactions under applicable statistical or regulatory rules. Screen all parties, banks, and jurisdictions against applicable EU and French sanctions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments and SWIFT customer credit transfers (commonly MT103-formatted messages, or the applicable ISO 20022 equivalent) for international payments, with accurate beneficiary, bank, invoice, contract, and payment-purpose data. Use irrevocable documentary commercial letters of credit, normally subject to UCP 600, when required by counterparties or project-finance documents; use documentary collections or guarantees only where contractually appropriate. Establish issuance limits, authorized signatories, dual approval, beneficiary verification, sanctions screening, document-checking procedures, and reconciliation controls. For trade settlement, retain contracts, invoices, transport and customs records, certificates of origin or inspection where relevant, and evidence supporting milestone payments. Agree currency, value date, fees, correspondent-bank charges, and allocation of FX risk in each contract. Bank acceptance, credit approval, collateral, and transaction-specific documentation are required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for documented or reasonably anticipated commercial exposures, subject to bank suitability, credit, and documentation requirements.
Non-deliverable forwards where the currency, counterparty, and transaction are legally eligible and settlement is permitted; these are not a substitute for any required underlying-exposure evidence.
Foreign-exchange swaps for liquidity and maturity management, subject to counterparty limits and applicable documentation.
Cross-currency swaps for appropriately documented financing or long-term cash-flow exposures, subject to bank approval and applicable derivatives documentation.

Options or other derivatives may be considered only where suitable for the company’s risk-management purpose and permitted by the counterparty’s product, classification, disclosure, and conduct requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du commerce et des sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,500 (natural person) or EUR 15,000 (legal person) for non-filing; after formal notice the public prosecutor or any interested party may request an injunction to file; persistent non-filing for multiple years triggers RCS radiation (strike-off) procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner annual confirmation / update (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual accounts; any shareholding or UBO change must be declared within 30 days of the transfer or event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of up to EUR 7,500 (natural person) or EUR 37,500 (legal person); failure to register shares may cause suspension of voting and dividend rights for those shares until the declaration is rectified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, déclaration de résultats n°2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, online return due on the second business day after 1 May; for other fiscal year-ends, due within 3 months and 15 days after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due, increased to 40% if not filed within 30 days of formal notice; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month; criminal sanctions in case of deliberate concealment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for an SAS that exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 4,000,000, net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000, or average employee count exceeding 50 for any one financial year. It is also mandatory if the SAS controls or is controlled by entities exceeding these thresholds, or if shareholders holding at least 10% of capital exercise their right to request an appointment before the annual meeting (no more than once in any five-year period).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, regulated by ANC and deriving from EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is required only for consolidated financial statements of listed parent entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual accounts deposit, the company must either confirm that the beneficial-owner data in the RBE remains unchanged or file an updated declaration. Declarations of share transfers must be lodged separately within 30 days; the annual confirmation does not cure a mid-year transfer. Until the registration is complete, the transferee's rights (dividends, voting) on the shares concerned may be suspended vis-à-vis the company, and sanctions for non-disclosure can reach EUR 37,500 for the legal entity.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des titres nominatifs)
Register of Decisions of the Sole Shareholder / General Meeting (registre des décisions de l'associé unique ou de l'assemblée)
Minute Book of consultations and written consultations of shareholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover < €10 million; Research Tax Credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; additional territorial and employment incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (income tax return) and 2065-SD (balance sheet) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending December 31, deadline is the second business day after May 1 of the following year; for other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months of year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report net profit after all adjustments and deductions; non-residents must include French-source income attributable to a permanent establishment.
Claim CIR, CII, and other eligible credits; non-residents may claim credits only if they have a French permanent establishment.
Report prior-year losses to offset current taxable income; non-residents must maintain proper documentation of loss carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax paid (Retenues à la source)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report any French withholding tax credits on income such as royalties or interest; non-residents must attach Form 5000 for treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of tax due, increased by 0.5% per month of delay, capped at 10%; plus interest at 0.2% per month on unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty, the beneficial owner must submit a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the recipient's jurisdiction, complete Form 5000 (or 5001 for dividends), and file with the French tax authority before the payment or within the statutory deadline for refund claims.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 33.33%, treaty rates often 0% or 5% depending on jurisdiction; Interest: statutory rate 30%, treaty rates often 0% or 10% depending on jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400 million (turnover or total assets) triggers mandatory Master File and Local File; also required if related-party transactions exceed €400 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies general anti-abuse rules and substance requirements for tax residency and treaty benefits; no specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) but requires real economic activity, personnel, and premises to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful understatement of taxable income, overstatement of deductions, or concealment of assets to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% on understated amounts, plus interest; criminal prosecution may result in fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they participated in or authorized fraudulent acts; civil restitution and potential travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a company without real economic substance (no employees, premises, or business activity) to artificially shift profits or obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, penalties up to 100% of tax avoided, and potential nullification of corporate status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for abusive tax arrangements, including fines and imprisonment for complicity in tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls, report suspicious transactions, or comply with customer due diligence requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for companies, and imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals; additional regulatory sanctions and license revocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned for AML violations; may also face civil liability for damages and travel bans.
